items.title: Disorder Festival reveals full lineup for 6-7 February 2027
items.summary: Disorder Festival revealed its full lineup for February 6-7, 2027, in Montreuil, adding And Also the Trees, VLURE, Yan Wagner and Paradox Obscur.
items.fullText:
Disorder Festival, a two-day event dedicated to the international goth, coldwave, darkwave, post-punk and EBM scenes, revealed its full lineup for February 6-7, 2027, in Montreuil, just outside Paris. The latest additions are And Also the Trees, VLURE, Yan Wagner and Paradox Obscur, joining the previously announced Martin Dupont, Frustration and David Shaw and the Beat. The event spans four venues in the same neighbourhood: La Marbrerie, Le Chinois, Le Bal Chavaux and La Bicyclette.

British post-punk band And Also the Trees formed in the early 1980s. Their album “Virus Meadow” marks its 40th anniversary in 2026, the same year the band released the album “The Devil’s Door.” VLURE contribute rave-punk, Yan Wagner brings dark pop, and Greek duo Paradox Obscur add electronic sounds to a lineup spanning post-punk, coldwave, darkwave and related genres.

Full lineup for Disorder Festival

Martin Dupont, Frustration, And Also The Trees, Corpus Delicti, Vlure, David Shaw And The Beat, Yan Wagner, Paradox Obscur, Abu Nein, Blind Delon, Body Shop, Heimberg, L’Écuyer, Laura Krieg, Lila Ejhä, Lone Assembly, Lunar Lock, Servo, SHV/ARZ, Talk To Her, The Spoiled, Theo Vandenhoff, Winter Severity Index and Years Of Shame.

Tickets for Disorder Festival are on sale via Shotgun.live.

About Disorder Festival

Disorder is a new festival built around the international goth, coldwave, darkwave, post-punk and EBM scenes, debuting in Montreuil on 6 and 7 February 2027 across four venues: La Marbrerie, Le Chinois, Le Bal Chavaux and La Bicyclette. Side-Line first covered the event’s inaugural fifteen-act announcement in October 2026, when organizers said a further wave of bookings would follow on October 30. That second wave has now confirmed And Also the Trees, VLURE, Yan Wagner and Paradox Obscur alongside the previously announced Martin Dupont, Frustration and David Shaw and the Beat, rounding out the full festival lineup. The event is organized with local press relations by Take Me Out.

items.title: Nitroverts release sophomore album ‘True Nature of Antimatter’
items.summary: Belarusian electro-metal duo Nitroverts released their sophomore album "True Nature of Antimatter" via FiXT on October 30, 2026, following 2023's "Endogenous".
items.fullText:
Belarusian electro-metal duo Nitroverts released their sophomore album, “True Nature of Antimatter,” on October 30, 2026, via FiXT. The eleven-track album follows 2023’s “Endogenous” and was written by Yann Zhanchak and Ars Nikonov, with vocals by Zhanchak and guitars, electronic programming, mixing and production by Nikonov, also known for his retro-synth project Fury Weekend. Cover art is by Nikonov.

The album combines alternative metal, nu metal, industrial rock, punk and hard rock across eleven tracks: “Under My Skin,” “Breakout,” “Unreal,” “Invincible,” “Dirt,” “Counterparts,” “Into Yesterdays,” “Spiral,” “Only One,” “Consent” and “Sirens.” A visualizer video for “Sirens” is out now via FiXT.

Nitroverts began in 2021 with the debut single “Starting Point,” followed by the debut album “Endogenous” in mid-2023. The duo released the EP “Into Yesterdays” in September 2025 and the single “Spiral” in April 2026 ahead of “True Nature of Antimatter.” FiXT, the album’s label, was founded in 2006 by Klayton (Celldweller) and James Rhodes.

“True Nature of Antimatter” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp and via FiXT’s other stores.

About Nitroverts

Nitroverts are an electro-metal duo from Minsk, Belarus, formed by vocalist Yann Zhanchak and multi-instrumentalist/producer Ars Nikonov, who also records retro synth music as Fury Weekend. The duo debuted with the single “Starting Point” in 2021, followed by their first album, “Endogenous,” in mid-2023. The EP “Into Yesterdays” followed in September 2025 and the single “Spiral” in April 2026, leading into their second album, “True Nature of Antimatter,” released October 30, 2026, via FiXT.

items.title: Ghostbells release ‘Phantoms’ single and video via Out Of Line Music
items.summary: Darkwave/EBM duo Ghostbells released the single and video "Phantoms" via Out Of Line Music on October 30, 2026, following "Curses" and "The Silence".
items.fullText:
Darkwave/EBM duo Ghostbells released the single and video “Phantoms” on October 30, 2026, via Out Of Line Music. The track follows “Curses” and “The Silence” as the latest step toward the duo’s debut full-length album.

The song centers on two people separated by death. “Phantoms is about two people who are bound by love into the afterlife. One person crosses over before the other, and the living eventually reunites with their lover,” the band stated. The track pairs icy new-wave melodies with a 1990s EBM pulse and club-ready production.

The release follows an extensive Latin America tour as direct support for label-mates Hocico. Earlier in the year, Ghostbells played Infest Festival in the UK and Dark Summer Open Air in Germany, supporting Blutengel and Chrom in front of an audience of around 3,000. The duo has also remixed Blutengel’s “Schwarzer Engel,” Cemetery Skyline’s “Torn Away” and Blitz Union’s “Evolution.”

Ghostbells have further dates in Texas and Florida this November, followed by Plage Noire Festival in Wangels and Obsidian Echoes Festival in Essen, and an appearance at Amphi Festival in Germany in 2027:

  • 13.11.2026 – Tampa, US, New World Tampa
  • 14.11.2026 – Miami, US, Las Rosas
  • 20.-21.11.2026 – Wangels, DE, Plage Noire Festival
  • 28.11.2026 – Essen, DE, Obsidian Echoes Festival
  • 24.-25.07.2027 – Cologne, DE, Amphi Festival

“Phantoms” is available to stream on Bandcamp and Spotify.

About Ghostbells

Ghostbells are a darkwave/EBM/synth-pop duo on Out Of Line Music. Side-Line has followed the band since the digital EP “Three Levels Of Dark And Dance” in December 2025, followed in 2026 by the singles “Curses” in August and “The Silence” in September. Earlier in 2026 the duo also released the EP “Catacouture.”

Across 2026 Ghostbells played Infest Festival in the UK and Dark Summer Open Air in Germany, where they supported Blutengel and Chrom, before touring Latin America as direct support for Hocico. The band has also remixed Blutengel’s “Schwarzer Engel,” Cemetery Skyline’s “Torn Away” and Blitz Union’s “Evolution.” A debut full-length album is in the works, following “Phantoms.”

items.title: Mark Springer and Jimmy Galvin play Bristol charity concert
items.summary: Mark Springer and Jimmy Galvin play a charity concert at The Mount Without in Bristol on November 26, 2026, benefiting the Bristol Drugs Project.
items.fullText:
British pianists and composers Mark Springer and Jimmy Galvin play a joint charity concert at The Mount Without in Bristol on November 26, 2026, with all proceeds going to the Bristol Drugs Project. Each performs solo and with a full string orchestra from the Bristol University Music Society, and Springer gives the live debut of material from “Sleep Of Reason,” his 2025 album written with Neil Tennant of the Pet Shop Boys and the Sacconi String Quartet, backed by a guest vocalist the promoters are keeping under wraps. Tickets for the 19:30 show are on sale now.

The bill also lists vocalist Kate Grant, performing as Isadora Vibes, among the night’s acts. Galvin, a Bristol-based composer and pianist, is also set to perform with the string orchestra and draw on his own catalogue, including his most recent album, “Spiritual Data,” released through Stoned Love Recordings.

“Sleep Of Reason” pairs Springer’s piano, string quartet and quintet arrangements with lyrics and vocals written by Tennant, developed after he read Francisco Goya’s print series “Los Caprichos” and its best-known image, “The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters.” The album runs in three parts: a six-track quintet section of voice and strings opening with “Phantoms And Monsters,” a three-track string-quartet set, and four solo-piano pieces to close. It was released through Sub Rosa and Exit Label in 2025.

“Looking up from my piano I see so much of the world that Neil has captured in his lyrics […] The words, Sleep of Reason, speak to the power hungry politics all around us and making this music now feels like my only rational move,” Springer said of the album. Tennant, who wrote the lyrics in response to Goya’s prints, described them as “sardonic and dreamlike, looking back to Goya’s nightmares but then reflecting on my experiences in 21st century popular culture and media.”

“Sleep Of Reason” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp, with CD and vinyl editions through Sub Rosa.

Jimmy Galvin is a Bristol-based composer, pianist and visual artist whose neo-classical music has drawn comparisons to Erik Satie, Bill Evans and Glenn Gould. He has released two solo piano albums, “A Million Seconds Make Eleven Days” and “Spiritual Data,” and performed the former live on BBC Radio 4’s “Loose Ends” in September 2018, to the show’s audience of around a million listeners. He has composed music for the BBC and Channel 4, including the independent film “Lido,” and exhibited paintings alongside artists including Peter Blake, Damien Hirst, Antony Gormley, Jake and Dinos Chapman and Mark Wallinger, with his work auctioned through Christie’s and Bonhams for charity. “Some of the most beautiful haunting original neo-classical music you will ever hear,” The New York Times said of his work. Galvin has organized a benefit concert of his own before: in 2021, he played a solo piano fundraiser for the Bristol Drugs Project at Bristol’s 15th-century St Stephen’s Church, the same charity the November 26 concert with Springer now supports.

About Mark Springer

Mark Springer is a British pianist and composer who first came to attention as a teenager in the experimental group Rip Rig + Panic, formed in 1981 with former Pop Group members Gareth Sager and Bruce Smith alongside singer Neneh Cherry. The group released three albums, “God,” “I Am Cold” and “Attitude,” before disbanding in 1983. Springer then began a solo career with the all-piano album “Piano,” released on Virgin Records in 1984, the first entry in a catalogue that has since moved between Virgin and Exit Records.

His Exit releases include “Nature/Music/Food/The Stars and The Planets” (2000), featuring drummer Clive Deamer, and he has worked extensively in opera and installation art. In 1994, he collaborated with artist Damien Hirst on “Agongo,” an opera installation staged at St Mary’s School during the Edinburgh International Festival. He wrote the music for “Army of Lovers,” an opera with a libretto by novelist David Flusfeder, which premiered at the Castello di Potentino in Tuscany in August 2018 and was staged at London’s Playground Theatre the following year.

“Sleep Of Reason,” Springer’s collaboration with Neil Tennant and the Sacconi String Quartet, followed in 2025 through Sub Rosa and Exit Label. The Bristol concert with Jimmy Galvin on November 26 gives the album its first live performance with a full string orchestra.

items.title: Llumen drops all new CD ‘Winter Eden’ on Alfa Matrix
items.summary: Llumen opens CD pre-orders for "Winter Eden", out 30 October 2026 on Alfa Matrix, also sold in a 3CD bundle with Implant and C-Lekktor.
items.fullText:
Belgian dark electronic project Llumen returns with its fourth album “Winter Eden” on Alfa Matrix. The digipak is sold on the label’s webstore; the twelve-track record is also sold digitally and as part of a three-way bundle with new albums from Implant and C-Lekktor.

Side-Line reported the album’s announcement in August, when Pieter Coussement confirmed the twelve-track running order and the lead single “The Leftovers”: Llumen announces fourth album ‘Winter Eden’ for 30 October, led by the single ‘The Leftovers’. “The Leftovers” was already released as a two-track single on Spotify.

Bundle pairs ‘Winter Eden’ with new Implant and C-Lekktor albums

The bundle package groups “Winter Eden” with Implant’s “The Kinematics Of Doubt” and C-Lekktor’s “Antimateria + C:file”, all three set for the same 30 October 2026 release date on Alfa Matrix. Llumen and Implant also share a double release party for their respective albums on 20 November 2026 at mOtown in Sint-Joost-ten-Node, Belgium, repeating a format the two acts first used for a joint Antwerp show in October 2021.

About Llumen

Llumen is the dark electronic project of Pieter Coussement, based in Ghent, Belgium. The act started out as a three-piece before Coussement continued alone from 2009, building a sound that layers old-school EBM, gothic textures, techno and future pop, with Front 242, Haujobb, Diorama, Assemblage 23, Suicide Commando and Covenant as declared reference points. The name itself is a nod to Front 242’s “U-Men”, a track Coussement later covered for the 2016 Alfa Matrix compilation “Recovery >For You< – An Alfa Matrix Tribute To Front 242”.

The debut album “The Memory Institute” reached an expanded bonus-tracks edition on 13 January 2017, and “Polygon Heart” followed on 18 June 2021, described by Coussement as his most autobiographical record after a health crisis reshaped his songwriting process. The nine-track EP “Die Stille Totgeschwiegen” arrived on 30 November 2023, covered at the time in Belgian electro act Llumen is back with 9-track EP ‘Die Stille Totgeschwiegen’ – Out now, and third album “The Breaking Waves” followed as a limited 2CD set on 17 May 2024, reported in Llumen is back with an all new album as a limited 2CD set and discussed at length in Llumen interview: ‘The Breaking Waves’ album acts as a reflection of inner turmoil.

Beyond his own catalogue, Coussement has produced official remixes for Noemi Aurora, C-Lekktor, Pre-Emptive Strike 0.1, Implant, Alien Vampires and Mildreda, contributed a version of Depeche Mode’s “Halo” to “Alfa Matrix Re:covered Vol. 3” in 2019 and covered Front 242’s “Gripped By Fear” for “Recovery 2 For You” in 2026. Live, Llumen performs as a three-piece and has played Infest, Mechanismus, Castle Party, BIMfest and electriXmas, most recently at Infest in Manchester in August 2025. “Winter Eden” is the project’s fourth studio album and its first full-length since “The Breaking Waves”, now confirmed for CD pre-order ahead of the 30 October release and the double release party with Implant.

items.title: Implant releases 15th album ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ on Alfa Matrix – Out now
items.summary: Implant releases the 15th studio album "The Kinematics Of Doubt" on CD and digital via Alfa Matrix on 30 October 2026, led by "Underneath The Neon Lights".
items.fullText:
Belgian EBM act Implant today released its 15th studio album “The Kinematics Of Doubt” on Alfa Matrix, thirty years after Len Lemeire started the project. The fourteen-track album is issued on CD and digital, and is also sold in a three-way bundle with new albums from Llumen and C-Lekktor.

The tracklist runs “The Observer Effect”, “Underneath The Neon Lights”, “Pills”, “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed”, “Civilization”, “Sanity”, “Framed”, “Transaction Failure”, “Are You Crying?”, “Talking In Your Sleep”, “Beyond The Code”, “No Apologies Required”, “On TV” and “Wounds”. Lemeire builds the album’s title from a term borrowed from physics, where kinematics describes movement without addressing the forces behind it; the label describes the record’s theme as doubt treated as motion rather than hesitation, running through songs about control, surveillance, obsession and identity. Lead single “Underneath The Neon Lights” carries the dancefloor pulse of the record, while “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” is built on a 3/4 rhythm, and “Pills”, “Framed” and “Sanity” work as more direct EBM cuts alongside the slower “Civilization”, “Talking In Your Sleep” and closer “Wounds”.

“Underneath The Neon Lights” is also available as a single on Spotify.

Double release party with Llumen on 20 November

Implant and Llumen launch their respective albums together on 20 November 2026 at mOtown in Sint-Joost-ten-Node, Belgium, repeating a format the two Belgian acts previously used for a joint release show in Antwerp in October 2021; Side-Line reported the date as part of Llumen’s “Winter Eden” announcement in LLUMEN announces fourth album ‘Winter Eden’ for 30 October, led by the single ‘The Leftovers’.

About Implant

Implant is the electro-industrial project Len Lemeire started in Belgium in 1996; that year’s debut CD single “Fun” credits Lemeire alongside Geert Machtelinck and was pressed in a numbered edition of 1,000 copies. Built on relentless EBM sequencing, physical electronics and a recurring catchphrase, “did you have your Implant today?”, the project has carried a catalogue that spans harsh EBM, industrial dance, electro-pop and dark synth across releases including “Implantology”, “Audio Blender”, “The Productive Citizen” and the EP “Fading Away”.

Implant released the free download single “The Drive” in December 2023, followed by the twelfth studio album “The Chaos Machines Part 1 – No More Flies On The Windscreen” in May 2024, a record Lemeire discussed in Implant interview: ‘Embrace chaos through the machines!’, where he described the album’s modular-synth approach and its duet with Noemi Aurora. The trilogy continued with the limited vinyl EP “The Chaos Machines Part 2 – Scratching The Surface” in September 2024 and closed with “Judging Sinners – The Chaos Machines Part 3” on 7 February 2025, a ten-track album again featuring Noemi Aurora and covered in a follow-up feature, Exclusive interview with Implant judging all those sinners. “The Kinematics Of Doubt” follows as Implant’s fifteenth studio album and, on Alfa Matrix’s account, its first release conceived outside that trilogy since 2024, arriving alongside the 20 November double release party with Llumen.

items.title: Test Dept and Brith Gof share ‘Arddylegog Ganu / Heroic Society’
items.summary: Test Dept and Brith Gof released the single "Arddylegog Ganu / Heroic Society" on October 30, 2026, ahead of the "Gododdin: 2026 Remaster" box set.
items.fullText:
London industrial group Test Dept and Welsh theatre company Brith Gof released the single “Arddylegog Ganu / Heroic Society (Early Studio Sessions, Reworked 2026)” on October 30, 2026 via Artoffact Records. The track is the second advance single from “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster,” a 3CD/1DVD box set expanding the pair’s 1989 album “Gododdin,” due December 4, 2026.

The single is accompanied by a video created by Jason Barton using footage from the stage premiere of “Gododdin” at an abandoned car factory in Cardiff, Wales, in December 1988. Test Dept founders Graham Cunnington and Paul Jamrozy built the new version from early studio session tapes, which the group says “were digitised and used as a template for a reworked version of the entire soundtrack.” The tapes carried early vocal takes later refined for the original album release, along with rhythmic material and samples not used on that version.

“Arddylegog Ganu / Heroic Society” follows the earlier advance single “Gwr A Aeth Gatraeth / Prologue (Early Studio Sessions, Reworked 2026),” both drawn from the sessions made for the original 1988 live soundtrack to “Gododdin.” The box set widens the original album’s seven tracks to 26, adding reworked studio sessions and a 1989 live recording from a quarry in Polverigi, Italy, plus a DVD documentary with footage and interviews. Full involvement came from Brith Gof members Lis Hughes Jones, John E R Hardy and Heike Roms, with audio remastered by Paul Lavigne at Kontrast Mastering and new artwork by Paul Jamrozy and Stefan Alt.

“Gododdin” is based on “Y Gododdin,” the earliest known poem in the Welsh language, telling of 300 Celtic warriors who fought a vastly larger invading force. Test Dept and Brith Gof’s staging combined live percussion and bagpipes with Brith Gof’s physical performance, music and Welsh-language vocals, premiering in Cardiff before further shows in Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland in 1989.

“Arddylegog Ganu / Heroic Society” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp, Spotify and Apple Music, ahead of the full “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” box set, which is open for pre-order as a 3CD/1DVD set and on red vinyl.

About Test Dept

Test Dept formed in London in 1981, building a reputation for percussion-driven industrial music performed on scrap metal and salvaged machinery alongside political and labour-movement themes. The group’s live soundtrack for “Gododdin,” created with Brith Gof and premiered in Cardiff in December 1988, ranks among the most important theatre events staged in Wales, touring Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland through 1989 before its studio recordings were released as an album in 1989, produced by Ken Thomas.

Test Dept signed to Artoffact Records in 2025 for a series of catalogue reissues and new material, beginning with the 4xCD “Industrial Overture” box set collecting early studio and live recordings, and the announcement of the “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” box set. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” is the second release in that reissue series, arriving a year after “Industrial Overture,” with new material from the band expected on Artoffact in 2027.

items.title: Coil’s ‘Gold is the Metal’ reissue arrives with ‘Cardinal Points’ video
items.summary: Coil's remastered reissue of "Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)" is out now via Mute and Threshold House, with a new "Cardinal Points" video.
items.fullText:
English experimental industrial act Coil‘s remastered reissue of “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is out now, October 30, 2026, via Mute and Threshold House, with vinyl and CD editions following on November 20. The release comes with a new video for “Cardinal Points,” built from footage of John Balance, Peter Christopherson and Stephen Thrower filmed in 1988 by René van der Eijk and directed by Alexander Oey for the program “Sound of Progress,” edited into the video by Ossian Brown and Davide Pepe.

“Gold is the Metal” is the first of four early Coil albums Mute and Threshold House are reissuing, each remastered with restored artwork, previously unseen imagery and new sleeve notes. The album is the third in a trilogy that began with “Scatology” and “Horse Rotorvator,” built from material sidelined during the sequencing of “Horse Rotorvator.” Stephen Thrower, who wrote the reissue’s new sleeve notes, describes it as “the culmination of a ‘magnum opus’ in the artistic sense, the closure of a trilogy – Scatology, Horse Rotorvator and Gold is the Metal – rounding up even our most jagged, cryptic, frictional, intemperate materials into a final balanced form.”

The album’s collage structure draws on field recordings including a brass band recorded in Mexico, a snippet of a British television documentary about young boxers, and a Thai boxing arena recorded by Christopherson. “Metal in the Head” preserves the sound of a hired Fairlight sampler malfunctioning and randomly distorting the music during recording.

Coil formed in London in 1982, when John Balance began using the name for a solo project. He had met Peter Christopherson, then a member of Throbbing Gristle, at a 1980 Throbbing Gristle show, and the two started performing as Coil in 1983 before leaving Psychic TV in January 1984 to work on the project full time. Their 1984 debut, the one-sided 12″ single “How to Destroy Angels,” was followed by Stephen Thrower joining as a full-time member from 1987 to 1992. On the reissue series, Coil are credited as Balance (1962-2004), Christopherson (1955-2010) and Thrower.

Threshold House was Coil’s own label, launched with “Gold is the Metal” in 1987. For this reissue, its artwork has been reconstructed by Thrower and his partner Ossian Brown, a member of Coil from 1999 to 2004, expanding on the original design with archive material including artefacts, photographs, artworks and personal notes made by Balance. Threshold House has been reactivated by Thrower and Brown for the new partnership with Mute, in association with the estates of Balance and Christopherson.

The series continues with Coil’s soundtrack for Derek Jarman’s “The Angelic Conversation,” the unreleased music Coil recorded for Clive Barker’s “Hellraiser,” and the compilation “Unnatural History.” Side-Line has tracked the reissue campaign since its announcement, including the expanded “Hellraiser” sessions and the earlier preview of the track “Either His, or Yours.”

“Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp, with vinyl and CD editions arriving November 20 through Mute.

About Coil

Coil formed in London in 1982 as a solo vehicle for John Balance, who had met Peter Christopherson, then a member of Throbbing Gristle, at a Throbbing Gristle concert in February 1980. After Throbbing Gristle dissolved in 1981, Christopherson joined Genesis P-Orridge in Psychic TV, where Balance also worked before the pair left in January 1984 to concentrate on Coil full time. Their debut release, the one-sided 12″ single “How to Destroy Angels,” came out that year on L.A.Y.L.A.H. Antirecords.

Stephen Thrower became a full-time member from 1987 to 1992, the period spanning “Scatology” (1985) and “Horse Rotorvator” (1986) on Some Bizzare, and “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” (1987), the first album on the band’s own label, Threshold House. “Love’s Secret Domain” followed in 1991. The 1990s also saw Balance and Christopherson work under aliases including Black Light District, ELpH and Time Machines.

Coil’s catalogue through 1999 and 2000 included “Astral Disaster,” “Musick to Play in the Dark Vol. 1,” “Queens of the Circulating Library” and “Musick to Play in the Dark Vol. 2,” followed by “Black Antlers” in 2004. John Balance died that November after a fall at his home; Peter Christopherson completed the band’s final studio album, “The Ape of Naples,” released in 2005, before his own death in Bangkok in 2010.

Side-Line has tracked Coil’s reissue catalogue, including the 10th-anniversary 2LP edition of “Backwards” and the 10th-anniversary “Recoiled” remix album with Nine Inch Nails. “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is the first release in the new reissue partnership between Mute and the reactivated Threshold House.

items.title: Ministry and Peter Hook cover Captain Beyond for ‘Thousand Days Of Yesterdays’ tribute
items.summary: Ministry and Peter Hook each cover "Dancing Madly Backwards" on Cleopatra Records' Captain Beyond tribute "Thousand Days Of Yesterdays," out November 20.
items.fullText:
Ministry and former New Order bassist Peter Hook each contribute a cover version to “Thousand Days Of Yesterdays – A Tribute To Captain Beyond,” a various-artists tribute album due November 20, 2026 via Cleopatra Records. Both acts rework the Captain Beyond signature track “Dancing Madly Backwards (On A Sea Of Air),” included as separate bonus tracks on the CD and digital editions. Ministry’s own next album, “Hate To Go,” is in the works, according to the label.

The tribute itself is built around the 1970s progressive/hard rock band Captain Beyond, a project formed by former Deep Purple vocalist Rod Evans with Iron Butterfly alumni Lee Dorman and Larry “Rhino” Reinhardt and drummer Bobby Caldwell, formerly of the Johnny Winter Group. “Thousand Days Of Yesterdays” reinterprets 19 songs from the band’s early catalogue, 13 of them on the blue vinyl edition, with contributions from Hawkwind’s Nik Turner, Thin Lizzy guitarist Brian Robertson, Pentagram, the Flower Kings, the Quill and others. The CD and digital editions add six further bonus tracks beyond the vinyl tracklist, including the Ministry and Hook versions.

The album marks Captain Beyond’s first full tribute collection, built around songs from the band’s self-titled 1972 debut and its following albums.

“Thousand Days Of Yesterdays” is available for pre-order as a digital album, CD and vinyl LP through Cleopatra Records’ Bandcamp page, due November 20, 2026.

About Ministry

Ministry is the industrial band led by Al Jourgensen, formed in Chicago in 1981. Starting out on a synthpop-leaning sound with the 1983 debut “With Sympathy,” the group shifted toward the heavier, sample-driven industrial metal style that defined albums such as “The Land of Rape and Honey” (1988), “Psalm 69” (1992) and “Filth Pig” (1996), and that has kept the band active across four decades of lineup changes around Jourgensen. Side-Line has tracked Ministry’s recent activity, including the reworked early-years compilation “The Squirrely Years Revisited” via Cleopatra Records and the “Dancing Alone” remix by Jurgen Engler. The band’s cover of Captain Beyond’s “Dancing Madly Backwards” arrives as its own next album, “Hate To Go,” is in development.

items.title: Wardruna releases ‘Helvegen II’, a new recording of ‘Helvegen’
items.summary: Wardruna released "Helvegen II," a new recording of "Helvegen" with a music film by Tuukka Koski, on October 30, 2026 via By Norse Music.
items.fullText:
Norwegian group Wardruna released “Helvegen II” on October 30, 2026 through By Norse Music, a new recording of “Helvegen,” one of the band’s best-known compositions since its original 2012 release. The track comes with a new music film directed by Finnish filmmaker Tuukka Koski, and the single is also available on colored 12″ vinyl.

Wardruna founder and composer Einar Selvik said the re-recording grew out of how the song has been used by listeners over the past fourteen years, including at funerals, weddings and births, and in communal singing traditions outside Scandinavia, now performed in multiple languages. “For some years now, we have been quietly working on a new recorded version of ‘Helvegen.’ Not to replace the original, but to reflect what the song has gradually become,” Selvik said.

In the music film, Finnish dancer Sofia Ruija portrays a deceased person through dance, accompanied by a raven named Krummi as a silent witness to the transition. “At some point, we realized that the song no longer existed only as the version we recorded in 2012. It had become something larger, shaped by the people who embraced it and by the countless moments in which it had been given a place and a purpose. This recording is our way of acknowledging that journey,” Selvik said.

The single carries two versions: “Helvegen II” and “Helvegen (Skaldic Version),” the latter exclusive to the vinyl edition.

“Helvegen II” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp, with the 12″ vinyl edition open for pre-order through the band’s own stores.

About Wardruna

Wardruna is a Norwegian group based in Bergen that builds its music around Nordic cultural and esoteric tradition, combining historical instruments and poetic metres with lyrics in Norwegian, Old Norse and related languages. The band’s sound took shape across the “Runaljod” trilogy – “Runaljod – gap var Ginnunga” (2009), “Runaljod – Yggdrasil” (2013) and “Runaljod – Ragnarok” (2016) – built around the 24 proto-Norse runes, before moving toward stripped-down, acoustic writing on “Skald” (2018). “Kvitravn” (2021), which explored Northern European magic, spirit animals and animism, reached number one in Canada and Austria and number two in Germany, among top chart placements in thirteen countries overall. A live album, “Kvitravn – First Flight of the White Raven,” followed in 2022, and the band’s most recent studio album, “Birna,” came out in 2025 to similarly strong chart results.

Founder, composer and multi-instrumentalist Einar Selvik grew up on the island of Osterøy north of Bergen, where an early interest in runes and Scandinavian history led him toward music rooted in historical sources after years in metal bands. He has studied pre-Christian Norse culture, philosophy and mythology since 2002, lectured on Old Norse history and music, and collaborated with artists including Mari Boine, Tina Guo, Matoma and Eivør. Outside Wardruna, Selvik composed music for the History Channel series “Vikings” (2014) and, with Jesper Kyd and Sarah Schachner, the soundtrack of the video game “Assassin’s Creed Valhalla” (2020).

Side-Line first covered Wardruna in 2020 around the announcement of “Kvitravn.” “Helvegen II” marks the band’s first new release since “Birna,” revisiting a song that has become one of its most personal to listeners since 2012.

items.title: Suicide Commando and Assemblage 23 unite on ‘I am your Darkness’
items.summary: Suicide Commando and Assemblage 23 release the single "I am your Darkness" via Out Of Line Music, with a five-track physical EP due December 3, 2026.
items.fullText:
Belgian electro-industrial act Suicide Commando and US EBM project Assemblage 23 released the collaborative single “I am your Darkness” on October 30, 2026 through Out Of Line Music. The digital release pairs a radio edit with an extended “Kill Your Demons” version. A five-track physical EP follows on December 3, 2026, available for pre-order now.

Suicide Commando mainman Johan Van Roy wrote the track as a confrontation with depression and self-doubt, set against pounding industrial rhythms and EBM programming. Assemblage 23 is the solo synthpop and EBM project of US musician Tom Shear, who joins Van Roy on the collaboration; Shear’s own project most recently released the album “Null” via Metropolis Records.

The lyrics present the inner voice of depression as an external presence, with lines such as “I am your darkness / I am your pain / I am your master / and I am your reign,” while the chorus, “Kill your demons / kill your fear,” reads as defiance, not resolution. “The song deals with depression and our constant fight against our own monsters and demons,” Van Roy and Shear said of the collaboration.

The physical EP adds three remixes: DSTRTD SGNL reworks the track for the dancefloor, label mate KLLSIGNL delivers a “Wendigo Cut,” and J Wølf contributes a further remix alongside the Kill Your Demons version, the radio edit and the DSTRTD SGNL mix.

“I am your Darkness” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp, with the physical EP open for pre-order there ahead of its December 3, 2026 release.

About Suicide Commando

Suicide Commando is the solo project of Belgian musician and producer Johan Van Roy, formed in 1986. Beginning with a series of self-released demo tapes in the late 1980s, the project has released music in the harder electro and EBM underground for four decades. The 1994 debut full-length “Critical Stage” started that run, followed by releases including “Mindstrip,” “Axis of Evil,” “Bind, Torture, Kill,” “Implements of Hell” and the 2022 album “Goddestruktor,” which reached number 9 on the official German album charts. Club tracks such as “See You in Hell,” “B.T.K.,” “Die Motherfucker Die” and “Hellraiser” remain staples of the dark electro scene.

Side-Line has tracked the project’s recent catalogue work, including the “Final Stage” EP revisiting the debut album, the 20th-anniversary reissue of “Axis of Evil” and the single “God Of Destruction.” Suicide Commando marks its 40th anniversary in 2026, the same year “I am your Darkness” brings Van Roy and Shear together for the first time.

items.title: Henrik Lysell on ‘I Think It Hurts’: ‘Don Juan Dracula show their slower, more personal side as they turn from red to black’
items.summary: Don Juan Dracula released the downtempo single "I Think It Hurts" on October 23, 2026. Henrik Lysell talks about the cover, the video and an album for 2027.
items.fullText:
(By our Norwegian correspondent Jan Ronald Stange. Photos by Tom Lund) Norwegian band Don Juan Dracula released “I Think It Hurts” on October 23, 2026 through Switch Off Records. The band usually mixes synthpop, rock and indie into energetic, catchy songs – the new single is a slower, more sombre downtempo track. The digital release pairs the original with a remix by Mörmaid.

Mörmaid is the project of Oslo-based producer, songwriter and vocalist Live Sollid Schulerud. She released her debut album “Pearlescent Dark” on May 23, 2024, and opened for Don Juan Dracula at Goldie in Oslo on May 23, 2025.

We’ve written before about their comeback single “Burn”, the SnifferGod rework of that track and the follow-up “Be The Same“, while realizing too late that their third single last year, “Play With Me“, went under the radar (slap on my hand for that!).

The new song differs from the previous releases in several ways, from the tempo to the cover and the video. In an email interview a week after the release, vocalist and songwriter Henrik Lysell talked about all three, as well as the band’s plans for 2027.

Interview: Henrik Lysell on Don Juan Dracula’s ‘I Think It Hurts’

Side-Line: The slower tempo, less playful, more serious-themed – is “I Think It Hurts” a new direction for DJD? Or complementing/balancing other songs?

Henrik Lysell: I wouldn’t really call it a new direction. I write quite a few slower songs, but they don’t all end up being released as singles or making it onto an album. We love playing upbeat music and getting a party going, but this is another side of Don Juan Dracula.

“I Think It Hurts” came about while I was sitting in the basement with my Moog Sub 37, singing whatever came out. I hadn’t written any lyrics beforehand. I just needed to get something off my chest, and this song was what came out of that.

There’s no doubt we’re entering a slightly darker period. The red is giving way to black, and the cover reflects that shift. But we’re still Don Juan Dracula, so there will always be a playful side to what we do.

Side-Line: The cover image breaks with previous styles – I think someone mentioned that it was a family member?

HL: The photo is actually of my grandmother, Eva, my dad’s mother. She’s no longer with us, and although she was always proud of me, she probably would have refused to let me use this particular photo on the cover! I loved her with all my heart, and she was a very important person in my life. I’ve always loved this picture. There’s something about it that I find visually beautiful, and it felt right for this song.

Side-Line: And the video is also quite different from the previous ones of the last few years; no AI, just getting ready to go on stage. What inspired that idea?

HL: Honestly, it started with a lack of time. We wanted to release the song now, and it needed a video, so we went back to footage from our show at Artilleriverkstedet last December, where we played to 400 people.

What I like about it is that you get to see behind the scenes, beyond the glossy AI videos and the stage personas. It’s us backstage, getting ready, being together. There’s a lot of friendship and love in this band, and I think that comes through. It doesn’t tell the story of the lyrics directly, but it shows the people behind the song. That felt right for something this personal.

Side-Line: How has the feedback on the release been so far?

HL: The feedback has been really good. People seem to appreciate hearing a slower, more vulnerable side of us. And the Mörmaid remix is insanely cool. We honestly couldn’t have asked for a better result. There will probably be more downtempo songs from us in the future too.

Side-Line: Any future plans and releases?

HL: Definitely. We have lots of songs nearly finished, so there’s plenty of new music coming, with an album planned for 2027. We’re incredibly proud of what we’re working on, and I don’t think we’ve ever felt more creative.

On December 12, we’re back at Artilleriverkstedet in Horten for our Christmas party show, just like last year, and we’re aiming for another packed house. Expect old favourites alongside plenty of new songs. The visual side is changing too, with the red giving way to black. You’ll see a slightly darker, more serious Don Juan Dracula, but we still know how to throw a party. See you at the show!

Tickets for Don Juan Dracula at Artilleriverkstedet on December 12, 2026

Stream “I Think It Hurts” here: Spotify | Apple Music | Deezer | Amazon Music | Tidal | YouTube Music | Pandora | iHeartRadio

About Don Juan Dracula

Don Juan Dracula come from Åsgårdstrand in Horten, Vestfold, and used Oslo as their home base in the early years. The band mixes guitar-based pop with synthesizers and electronics, and performs in white suits. The first official release, the “Perfect Girl EP”, came out on Switch Off Records on February 11, 2002, with songs by vocalist and guitarist Henrik Lysell and keyboardist Henning Krane, and Ola Eriksen on bass. The “Happy Boy EP” followed on April 28, 2003.

With Thomas Lute on drums, the band recorded the debut album “Young Debutantes II” with producer Alex Møklebust of Seigmen and Zeromancer, mostly at the band’s own rehearsal studio. Switch Off Records released it on March 7, 2005, shortly after the “Take Me Home EP”, a remix release built around the album’s lead single. On August 12, 2005, Don Juan Dracula opened Øyafestivalen in Oslo by landing in a rented helicopter next to the stage while their local school band played.

After the tour for the album, the band took a short break, then returned in 2006 with shows in New York and at Beijing Pop Festival, where Placebo and Supergrass were also on the bill. The second album, “New Sensation”, followed on June 23, 2008. The band recorded and produced it themselves, with mixing by Ed Buller and Stephen Hague. It remained their last release for almost 17 years.

The comeback started on February 14, 2025 with the self-produced single “Burn”, with Fredrik Fagerli Dahle as the new drummer. Møklebust remixed the track as SnifferGod in March 2025, and “Be The Same” came out on April 11, 2025.

On May 23, 2025, the band played Goldie, their first Oslo concert in 17 years. “Play With Me”, with the B-side “Bloquée”, followed on October 31, 2025, and on December 13, 2025 the band played a Christmas show at Artilleriverkstedet in Horten.

The current lineup is Henrik Lysell (vocals, guitar), Henning Krane (synth), Ola Eriksen (bass), Fredrik Fagerli Dahle (drums) and Dino Trto (guitar). “I Think It Hurts” is the band’s first release of 2026, arriving a year after “Play With Me”. Don Juan Dracula plan an album for 2027 and return to Artilleriverkstedet on December 12, 2026.

items.title: The Klinik’s ‘Box’ reissued on triple vinyl by Antler Records
items.summary: The Klinik's 1990 compilation 'Box' returns on October 30, 2026 as a remastered triple-vinyl edition through Antler Records, the label's original home.
items.fullText:
The Klinik’s compilation “Box” returns on October 30, 2026 as a remastered triple-vinyl edition through Antler Records, the label that first released it in 1990. The set brings together 19 tracks that Marc Verhaeghen and Dirk Ivens recorded between 1984 and 1988 at The Lab, a period in which the duo developed the cold, stripped-down electronic sound that the band became known for within the Belgian EBM scene. Music on the original recordings is credited to Verhaeghen, lyrics to Ivens.

The original “Box” sold out in its limited pressing and became a sought-after collector’s item; it was later reissued on Hands Productions in 2004. This new edition comprises three heavyweight black 12-inch records in an expanded single sleeve carrying the original front cover, with a double-sided printed inner sleeve featuring previously unpublished photographs by Inge Bekkers. The recordings were digitally remastered by Pieter De Wagter (Equus) in 2026. “Box” is available to pre-order through Antler Records.

About The Klinik

The Klinik was formed in Belgium around 1982 by Marc Verhaeghen. In 1985, Verhaeghen, Dirk Ivens and Eric van Wonterghem of Absolute Body Control joined Sandy Nijs of The Maniacs under the name Absolute Controlled Clinical Maniacs, soon shortened to The Klinik. Nijs left the following year to form Hybryds, and van Wonterghem left in 1987, leaving Ivens and Verhaeghen as the duo behind the band’s best-known work, released through Antler.

The Klinik’s 1991 album “Time” was the last the Ivens/Verhaeghen duo made together before the pair went separate ways; Ivens went on to form Dive, while Verhaeghen continued the project, dropping “The” from its name. Ivens and Verhaeghen reunited for live shows in 2003 and 2004, and again for the album “Eat Your Heart Out” in 2013, their first studio album together in 22 years. Side-Line reported in 2017 that the band remained active without Ivens.

items.title: Abu Nein releases ‘Ghost Puppeteer’ single
items.summary: Abu Nein released 'Ghost Puppeteer' on October 30, 2026 via Icons Creating Evil Art, the first single from the upcoming album 'Is Anyone Awake?'
items.fullText:
Malmö darkwave act Abu Nein released “Ghost Puppeteer” on October 30, 2026 via Icons Creating Evil Art, the first of three singles leading up to their new album “Is Anyone Awake?,” due February 5, 2027. The 3:39 track combines driving electronics and synthpop hooks with a theme centred on autonomy and cutting ties, and includes a baile funk-styled “Ye Ardina” vocal sample through its chorus.

“Ghost Puppeteer” was produced by Erica Li Lundqvist and Tobias Bernstrup, who also wrote the music between them; Lundqvist wrote the lyrics, Bernstrup mixed the track and Doruk Özturkcan handled mastering. The single follows a line-up change that leaves Lundqvist as the band’s sole remaining songwriter, working alongside Bernstrup to shape the group’s next chapter.

“Ghost Puppeteer” is available on Spotify.

About Abu Nein

Abu Nein debuted in 2020 with “Secular Psalms,” an album nominated for a Manifest Award and winner of the Synthsläggan Award for Best Swedish Debut Album. The band’s third album, “III: Dark Faith,” won the Manifest Award for Best Swedish Synth Album. Abu Nein has performed across Scandinavia and Europe, including Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Amphi Festival, NCN Festival and Prague Gothic Treffen, and has shared stages with Kite, The Legendary Pink Dots, Minuit Machine and She Past Away.

Reviewers have described the band’s sound as “Speak and Spell era Depeche Mode if Siouxie Sioux replaced Dave Gahan,” according to ReGen Magazine, and as “an artful take on modern Darkwave, fueled by evocative and melancholic gothic-infused Post-punk poetry,” according to White Light // White Heat.

items.title: Melbourne’s Ohms Serves up a Grotesque Feast of Mutant Post-Punk in Video for “Aeroplane Jelly”
items.summary: Beg your Mum and Dad, beg them for a treat. Scrounge around like vultures, picking remnants left from meat. Boil and grind ‘em to a pulp, Draining blood for me… The post Melbourne’s Ohms Serves up a Grotesque Feast of Mutant Post-Punk in Video for “Aeroplane J
items.fullText:
Beg your Mum and Dad, beg them for a treat.

Scrounge around like vultures, picking remnants left from meat.

Boil and grind ‘em to a pulp, Draining blood for me to gulp,

Hydrolize what’s left to form a collagenic clump.

Imagine a children’s birthday party where the jelly starts talking back, the cake develops a nervous disorder, and somebody discovers that the dessert contains enough pulverized animal remains to make a slaughterhouse accountant reconsider his career. Such is the splendidly sick premise behind Aeroplane Jelly, the latest offering from Melbourne’s Ohms, whose principal troublemaker, Lachlan P. Rother, appears determined to investigate precisely how much musical lunacy can occupy three minutes before the recording equipment files a formal complaint.

Rother, formerly the ringleader of U-Bahn and currently dividing his time between GLASNOST and High Control Group, has developed an appetite for musical mischief that would make Frank Zappa raise an approving eyebrow. Here, the gloriously primitive aggression of The Stooges collides with Thee Oh Sees at their most unhinged, while the early psychedelic experiments of King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard provide further evidence that Australian musicians have been consuming something considerably stronger than ordinary breakfast cereal.

The guitars buzz with the persistence of flies circling a butcher’s counter, while the drums administer a merciless beating beneath bass synthesizers that seem afflicted by some terrible digestive complaint. Above this mechanical bedlam, Rother’s heavily manipulated falsetto squeals and squirms, occasionally attaining the emotional composure of a laboratory rat discovering electricity.

Then comes the magnificent descent into outright absurdity. Bubblegum synthesizers and combo organs turn the proceedings into a deranged fairground attraction, complete with the sort of artificial cheerfulness ordinarily reserved for television advertisements promising children that industrially processed sugar constitutes a balanced breakfast. Fans of Suburban Lawns will recognize the same appetite for making pop music behave very badly indeed.

Beneath all this splendid stupidity sits a genuinely spicy little observation about the modern food industry. Rother examines gelatine production through images of boiled bones, extracted marrow, pulverized connective tissue, and sugary camouflage, transforming a beloved childhood dessert into a grisly metaphor for consumption, exploitation, and humanity’s astonishing willingness to swallow practically anything provided somebody makes it colorful and inexpensive.

The joke becomes increasingly uncomfortable once you realize how closely the grotesque descriptions resemble ordinary manufacturing procedures. Advertising supplies the smiling cartoon characters; the factory supplies the collagen. Everybody gets dessert, provided nobody asks too many questions.

Filmed in Peru in 2026 and directed by Triana Hernandez, the video turns a Chinese restaurant into the setting for an exceptionally dubious dinner service. Beneath red lighting and paper lanterns, Calcio, wearing a stained shirt and apron, cuddles a cake with a face, brandishes kitchen utensils, and attacks a karaoke microphone as though his continued employment depends upon it. Victor Torer’s camera tilts and spins past aquarium fish and restaurant ornaments, while vintage cartoons of the Three Little Pigs and the Big Bad Wolf interrupt the proceedings. Their familiar chase acquires an unpleasantly practical meaning alongside the song’s inventory of animal ingredients.

A pig’s head presides over the banquet as extreme close-ups and bursts of television static make the whole affair resemble a VHS cooking programme whose host has lost all interest in repeat customers. The closing mock commercial completes the joke: an enormous German instruction to call now fills the screen alongside a telephone number ending in 666. Childhood treats, cartoon predators, and hard selling all arrive on the same platter, with the cheerful presentation doing its best to distract from what is actually being served.

As the final single preceding Ohms’ debut album, Wechselströme, Aeroplane Jelly presents Rother at his most wonderfully deranged, juggling garage rock, mutant post-punk, psychedelic excess, and cartoonish electronic experimentation with the enthusiasm of a man conducting dangerous experiments in his kitchen.

Consider the ingredients carefully before reaching for another helping.

items.title: Baltes & Zäyn release ‘Bride of Frankenstein’ single
items.summary: Baltes & Zäyn released the tech-noir electro single 'Bride of Frankenstein' on October 31, 2026 via Echozone, a horror-themed Halloween release.
items.fullText:
Baltes & Zäyn released “Bride of Frankenstein” on October 31, 2026 via Echozone. The tech-noir electro single is built around the mad-scientist trope of the 1935 Universal film of the same name, directed by James Whale as a sequel to his 1931 film “Frankenstein,” and starring Boris Karloff with Elsa Lanchester as the Bride.

The song’s lyrics were written by ZÄYN in 1988. The instrumental was sketched in 2023 on a vintage Yamaha QY-700 hardware sequencer and completed by BALTES the same year. “Bride of Frankenstein” follows the duo’s earlier single built around a crossover between a Godzilla-style kaiju and Fritz Lang’s “Metropolis,” continuing the pair’s recurring use of horror and science-fiction film references, and arrives timed for Halloween.

About Baltes & Zäyn

Baltes & Zäyn release tech-noir electro through the German label Echozone, with a recurring focus on horror and science-fiction film imagery across their singles, including the kaiju-themed single that preceded “Bride of Frankenstein.”

items.title: The Grab Society releases ‘Eternal (Halloween Mix)’ single
items.summary: The Grab Society released 'Eternal (Halloween Mix)' on October 30, 2026 via Echozone, an extended radio-play edition of their 2024 single 'Eternal.'
items.fullText:
The Grab Society, the duo of Manfred Thomaser and Ulf Müller, released “Eternal (Halloween Mix)” on October 30, 2026 via Echozone. The single expands the group’s earlier track “Eternal,” released close to two years ago, into a Halloween-themed edition centred on a vampire narrative, again featuring Lady Annabelle alongside Jörg Tochtenhagen.

The release sets a spoken radio-play segment inside the song, extending the track to a run time of close to 43 minutes. The tracklist comprises “Eternal (Halloween Mix feat. Annabelle & Jörg Tochtenhagen)” and an instrumental version of the same mix. The cover artwork was AI-generated by Julian Blaustein together with The Grab Society. The single’s release, timed for Samhain and All Hallows’ Eve, continues the narrative thread of the original “Eternal,” giving its protagonist a second life within the story.

About The Grab Society

The Grab Society is the project of Manfred Thomaser and Ulf Müller, releasing dark electro and electropop through the German label Echozone. Lady Annabelle and Jörg Tochtenhagen, both credited on “Eternal (Halloween Mix),” have contributed to the group’s work before, on the original version of “Eternal.”

items.title: Endzustand releases ‘Human Kapital’ single via Echozone
items.summary: Endzustand released the EBM single 'Human Kapital' on October 30, 2026 via Echozone, the second single from the album 'Macht Gesellschaft.'
items.fullText:
Endzustand released “Human Kapital” on October 30, 2026 via Echozone, the second single from the EBM act’s current album “Macht Gesellschaft.” The track is out as a digital single with three remixes attached, by Wellencocktail (Achim Dreßler), Genom Staahl and Plastikstrom.

“Human Kapital” addresses the value of the individual in a society where, as the band’s own description puts it, millions work daily while a small number profit and continue to accumulate wealth. The lyrics treat work, performance and availability as metrics that reduce a person to an economic figure, without offering a slogan or rallying cry in response.

About Endzustand

Endzustand is an EBM act on the German label Echozone. Its current line-up is Ralle on vocals and Rudi on drums.

“Human Kapital” is the second single pulled from the band’s album “Macht Gesellschaft,” and arrives with the three remixes from Wellencocktail, Genom Staahl and Plastikstrom.

items.title: SRK Group releases ‘Bleeding Heartsicle’ via Infacted Recordings
items.summary: SRK Group, Sebastian R. Komor's new project, released the single 'Bleeding Heartsicle' on October 30, 2026 via Infacted Recordings.
items.fullText:
SRK Group, the dark electro project of producer Sebastian R. Komor, released the single “Bleeding Heartsicle” on October 30, 2026 via Infacted Recordings. The release date was set for Halloween, and the single’s artwork carries the SRK Group logo rendered in dripping orange lettering.

“Bleeding Heartsicle” is SRK Group’s second release. The project debuted on September 11, 2026 with “Spitfire”, also via Infacted Recordings, which Komor wrote, produced, mixed and mastered at his own Xenomorph Production Studio. Like its predecessor, “Bleeding Heartsicle” keeps SRK Group in dark electro and EBM, built for club play.

“Bleeding Heartsicle” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp.

About SRK Group

SRK Group is the newest outlet for Sebastian R. Komor, a Polish-born, Norwegian-raised producer now based in Canada who has spent around three decades in the electronic underground. Komor is best known as a longtime member of Icon of Coil, and his project history also includes Monofader, Zombie Girl, Komor Kommando, Moonitor and Melt. Through Bruderschaft, he worked alongside Ronan Harris of VNV Nation, Joakim Montelius of Covenant and Stephan Groth of Apoptygma Berzerk.

Beyond his own projects, Komor has built an extensive catalogue as a producer, remixer, mixer and mastering engineer, crediting work with Apoptygma Berzerk, Front Line Assembly, Ayria, Glis, Circle of Dust, Clockwork Echo, Soft Vein and SPANKTHENUN, among others, and he has also remixed material for Aesthetic Perfection.

SRK Group launched on September 11, 2026 with “Spitfire,” a track combining dark electro, EBM and club-oriented electronics that Komor described at the time as “personal, loud and danceable.” “Bleeding Heartsicle,” released seven weeks later, is the project’s second single.

items.title: Obychno Odyn Confronts State Control in Video for Spectral Coldwave Single “Погибель” — New Album “Адинамия” Out Now!
items.summary: Я не могу вздохнуть в своей же квартире Мне суждено быть осуждённым в этом мире Внушая громко правила в громкоговоритель они ведут тебя на погибель A voice through a loudspeaker… The post Obychno Odyn Confronts State Control in Video for Spectral Coldwave Sing
items.fullText:
Я не могу вздохнуть в своей же квартире
Мне суждено быть осуждённым в этом мире
Внушая громко правила в громкоговоритель
они ведут тебя на погибель

A voice through a loudspeaker can make even a private room feel like government property. It gives instructions, announces obligations, and leaves the person listening to wonder how much of their own life they are still permitted to keep. The promises of protection become difficult to believe when those making them have already decided whose lives they can afford to lose.

Turin-based coldwave and post-punk project Obychno Odyn confronts this dynamic on “Погибель” (“Doom”), the opening track of its new album, Адинамия (adynamia or profound exhaustion). Ukrainian musician Vadym Protsenko depicts a government that claims ownership over everything, ready to sacrifice the people in its grasp to safeguard its own dark ambitions. 

An echoing snare splash establishes an uneasy beat, its accents suggesting an irregular heartbeat. Above it, a high, desolate guitar melody keeps circling, lending the song a funereal sway. A second, more spectral line curls around the first, drawing the arrangement towards gothic rock without relieving its starkness. Protsenko’s voice spreads through the reverb until one singer seems to contain a procession of monks, each phrase answered by its own retreating echo. It sounds like Trop Tard if they were haunting a monastery, the music finding ample room to reverberate while its singer struggles for air.

The Russian-language lyrics carry that pressure into the home: the right to stand, to smile, even to breathe within one’s own apartment rests in someone else’s hands. Those who seized power with weapons at their sides issue commands as people die and fragile hands are bound. Passers-by keep moving, inured to the same abuses, while the machinery grinds on, day after day. The closing lines cast a glance across centuries of wars, killings, and prison terms, placing vast troubles beside the meager answers of leaders absorbed in their own affairs. For those trapped beneath them, a whole lifetime may pass with no way out.

The video gives that confinement a physical setting. Protsenko faces the camera beside barred windows, at points delivering his words through a megaphone. Elsewhere, guitar and bass are played beneath the harsh yellow light of a streetlamp, surrounded by trees and darkness. Grainy monochrome passages, glimpses of stone figures, and diagonal bands of green interference interrupt the performance. Close-ups bring faces and instruments within reach, but the bars and degraded picture keep obstructing the view. Even outdoors, there is little sense of release.

Watch the video for “Погибель” below:

Protsenko founded Obychno Odyn in Bucharest in 2025, responding to upheaval internationally and in his home country through songs concerned with war, existence, and emotional isolation. His writing in Russian and English draws on French coldwave from the 1980s, particularly Trop Tard and Bunker Strasse. The eight-song debut album Излияние (“Outpouring”) followed in 2026. For live performances, bassist Marcello Aloisio joins Protsenko on vocals and guitar.

Ahead of this release, Post-Punk.com premiered “Уходят люди и часы” (“People and Hours Pass”) and “Мир угасает во тьме” (“The World Fades into Darkness”). The former examined the uncertainty of human connection; the latter gave physical form to exhaustion beneath an increasingly oppressive world. “Погибель” directs that accumulating distress towards the authorities who demand obedience while treating human life as expendable.

Адинамия is out now. Listen to the album below and order here.
